description: We’re a student team from Universiti Teknologi Malaysia (UTM) Johor Bahru participating online in NASA Space Apps 2026. Most of us master Computer Science foundation skills and have participate few hackathons established in local. We’ve worked together at hackathons and tech events. We’re building a fun, beginner-friendly Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer game about managing a lunar base. We welcome remote teammates interested in coding, UI/UX, space science, storytelling or pitching.
summary: AstroBase: Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer is a browser-based 2D outpost survival game for learners ages 7–12. Players select a Moon or Mars site, allocate limited power among life support, radiation shielding, hydroponics and communications, complete workstation mini-games, respond to mission events, and track oxygen, food, cumulative radiation and science over a seven-Sol mission. A deterministic survival model turns those choices into resource changes, warnings and mission outcomes. The fixed gameplay schedule is a curated scenario informed by historical NASA DONKI events; separate reference panels can retrieve live DONKI, NASA OSDR and RadLab data, NASA imagery and Perseverance rover photos, with archived or fallback content when services are unavailable. Canadian Space Agency STEM references connect food-production activities to educational resources. Optional Gemini-powered features can generate mission events, transcribe voice input, provide commander replies and compose adaptive music when configured. Live feeds do not replace the fixed seven-Sol gameplay schedule, and simulation values are simplified educational approximations.
details:
AstroBase is an interactive 2D mission-survival game designed for learners ages 7–12. Players choose a Moon or Mars outpost and manage a seven-Sol mission by allocating limited power across life support, radiation shielding, hydroponics and communications. They interact with eight workstation areas, including power, oxygen and filter systems, crop growing, food preparation, shielding, rover/EVA operations, communications and an educational quiz station. Workstation activities and mission choices affect oxygen, food, cumulative radiation dose and science score. The mission ends in success after seven Sols or an emergency abort if oxygen or food is depleted or the radiation limit is reached.

The application is built with React, TypeScript, Vite, Tailwind CSS and an Express/Node.js server. Firebase Authentication and Firestore support optional cloud mission logs and saved settings; local storage supports local logs. Optional Google Gemini features can generate mission events and adaptive music, and support voice transcription and commander replies when the required service configuration is available.

NASA reference panels include DONKI, OSDR and RadLab, NASA imagery, Mars rover photos, and Moon/Mars Trek maps. The game’s seven-Sol scenario and resource calculations are fixed and simplified for education. They are not live mission forecasts or validated engineering models.
